failures.criterion: The note's instrument advice is the measured one (spec acceptance 1, the criterion round 1 failed on): the corrected bullet names a `df` flag that does not exist in the sense it implies.
failures.evidence: docs/solutions/testing/a-pod-harness-moves-tmpdir-too-and-the-failure-mode-is-a-silent-kill-INFRA-44.md:138-139 reads '`du -x` and `df -x` are the ones to avoid here', putting `df -x` beside `du -x` as the one-filesystem walk to avoid. GNU df has no such flag: `-x` is `--exclude-type=TYPE` and takes an argument. Measured in the INFRA-69 tester container at head 925cac4e999429904180b78ab5b204debdf29cda: `df -x` prints `df: option requires an argument -- 'x'` with `Try 'df --help' for more information.` and exits 1; `df -x /` is read as 'exclude filesystems of type /', excludes nothing, exits 0 and prints 21 lines — the header and every one of the container's 20 mounts, `/legion`, `/home/legion/.config` and all seven `/var/run/legion/*` among them. So the clause is false in both readings: the command a reader would type either errors or does the opposite of restricting the view. The real `df` hazard here is the one the note already avoids by naming `/`: `df` answers for the filesystem of the path it is given, so `df /legion` or `df ~/.cache` reports that path's own filesystem rather than the 1 GiB budget. Fix: drop `df -x` from the clause, leaving `du -x` as the one to avoid, or replace it with that real caveat. The same clause is in the PR body's `E2E (implementer)` line ('avoid `du -x` and `df -x`'), which this repository squashes into main's commit message, so it needs the same edit. No repository test pins it: the repository has no checker over docs/solutions/ prose, and a grep over wording is a source-text test its conventions forbid; the two commands above are the re-runnable evidence.
